answer: Eccentricity-Anchored Placement. Each identity must occupy a distinct vertex whose neighbor set differs from every existing member by a fixed Hamming margin; the registry accepts a join only if the new node's local connectivity signature is novel, so clones sharing a parent collapse into one slot. Maintaining that margin costs an attacker a dedicated lotus of distinct links per identity, forcing real fan-out rather than cheap replication, and each forged jade of connectivity must stay live or the vertex is pruned.
